rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Newton's law of cooling tells you the exact time of death. ✅ It gives an ESTIMATE. The model ignores many factors (clothing, body size, air movement, humidity) that affect real cooling rates.  ·  ❌ The law works equally well for very large temperature differences (e.g., a red-hot iron in air). ✅ For large $\Delta T$, radiation ($\propto T^4$) dominates over convection, and Newton's linear law becomes inaccurate.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ A larger object always cools faster. ✅ Larger objects have larger heat capacity ($mc$), which slows cooling. The cooling RATE depends on the ratio $k/(mc)$, not just on size.  ·  ❌ Newton's law of cooling is the same as the Stefan-Boltzmann law. ✅ Newton's law is linear ($d\theta/dt \propto \theta - \theta_0$). Stefan-Boltzmann is quartic ($\propto T^4 - T_0^4$). Newton's law is an approximation valid for small $\Delta T$.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Newton's law of cooling is an example of a "linear first-order differential equation" — the same mathematical form appears in RC circuits ($dQ/dt = -Q/RC$), radioactive decay ($dN/dt = -\lambda N$), and chemical reaction kinetics.  ·  The time constant $\tau = mc/k$ has units of time and appears in countless physical, chemical, and biological processes. It characterizes how "inertial" a thermal system is — large $\tau$ means slow response.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: **Purpose of Newton's law of cooling:** The law provides a simple mathematical model to predict how the temperature of a body changes with time when it is placed in a surroundings of constant temperature.  ·  **Forensic science — estimating time of death:** A corpse cools according to Newton's law after death (the "algor mortis" process). If body temperature is measured at time $t$, and the ambient temperature is known, the law estimates how long ago death occurred: $\theta(t) = \theta_0 + (\theta_{body} - \theta_0)e^{-K't}$.  ·  **Engineering — cooling system design:** Engineers use Newton's law to size radiators, heat sinks, and cooling fans. For a component dissipating power $P$, the steady-state temperature rise is $\Delta T = P/(kA)$, where $k$ is the heat transfer coefficient.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Concept 5: Connection between Newton's Law of Cooling and other topics  ·  ❌ The cooling constant $k$ is a property of the material. ✅ $k$ depends on the SURFACE properties (area, texture, air flow), not the material inside. Two objects of the same material but different shapes have different $k$.  ·  ❌ Once a body reaches room temperature, it stays there forever. ✅ It reaches thermal equilibrium asymptotically — it gets arbitrarily close but never exactly reaches $\theta_0$ in finite time (though for practical purposes it appears to).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ❌ The method of cooling (comparing cooling rates) gives the exact specific heat. ✅ It gives an approximate value. Errors arise from non-identical conditions, radiation losses, and the approximation that $k$ is constant.  ·  Carefully distinguish between similar-looking concepts in newton's law of cooling.  ·  Pay attention to the conditions under which formulas and theorems apply.
